title: SDK: expose resolved model_version + changelog_url in responses; update docs/examples
author: Ibrahim Khan
description:
Context: Customers want to understand which model version actually served a request (esp. during rollouts/canaries) and to have a stable link to customer-visible release notes. The control plane now provides resolved model version metadata + changelog URL (see ENG-4928 / openai-compat work). This PR plumbs that data through the Python SDK so app teams can log/trace it and link it into their own change-management workflows.

What this PR does: 1) Adds typed fields to response objects for chat/completions/responses endpoints: `model_version` (string) and `changelog_url` (string | None). 2) Captures the values from Redwood-specific response headers when present (non-breaking for generic OpenAI-style responses). 3) Surfaces the fields consistently across streaming and non-streaming codepaths. 4) Updates docs + examples to show printing the resolved version and linking to release notes.

API details: - Header parsing: `X-Redwood-Model-Version` and `X-Redwood-Model-Changelog-Url`. - SDK response fields: `response.model_version` and `response.changelog_url` (mirrored onto `ChatCompletion`/`Completion` wrappers for backward compat). - Streaming: fields are set once headers are available; for generators we attach them to the final aggregated object returned by `stream.final_response()`.

Why headers (vs body): This matches the OpenAI-compat gateway behavior and avoids polluting upstream JSON schemas; also allows existing pinned-version behavior to remain unchanged.

Docs: Added a short section under "Version pinning" clarifying the difference between requested model vs resolved model_version and linking to the model changelog feed.

Test coverage: - Unit tests for header parsing, None handling, and ensuring we do not raise if headers are missing. - Streaming integration test fixture validates that fields are available on the aggregated response.

Notes / follow-ups: - This PR does not add a first-class changelog client; it only surfaces the URL. - Once the docs site feed is GA, we may add helper methods to fetch and cache changelog entries in a future PR.
commits: sdk: parse Redwood model metadata headers and attach to response objects
sdk: add model_version + changelog_url fields to types and public docs
tests: cover header parsing and streaming aggregation behavior
examples: log resolved model version + link to changelog
changed_files: src/redwood/_http.py (capture response headers and attach to response context)
src/redwood/resources/responses.py (plumb fields into Responses API wrapper)
src/redwood/streaming.py (ensure aggregated final response retains metadata)
illustrative_snippet:
Example usage (docs/examples):

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="rw-llama-3.1-70b",
    input="Summarize the incident timeline."
)
print("resolved:", resp.model_version)
if resp.changelog_url:
    print("release notes:", resp.changelog_url)

# resolved: rw-llama-3.1-70b@2026-02-18
# release notes: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/model-release-notes/rw-llama-3.1-70b/2026-02-18
conversation:
Monica Patel (review): Can we confirm field names match the gateway? Also please ensure missing headers don’t break non-Redwood endpoints.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Confirmed with Brian: `X-Redwood-Model-Version` and `X-Redwood-Model-Changelog-Url` are what openai-compat is emitting. Added defensive parsing + tests where headers are absent.

Brian Murphy (review): Please avoid injecting these into the JSON payload for OpenAI compat; headers-only is correct. One nit: normalize header lookup case-insensitively.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated `_http.py` to treat headers as case-insensitive and added a regression test.

Elliot Price (review): Docs wording: avoid saying “model was upgraded” — better “resolved model version served this request”. Also add a sentence that changelog entries may be delayed during beta.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated docs copy to match style guide language and added a short beta caveat.

Wei Chen (review): Example is good; can we include a note on logging these into traces?

Ibrahim Khan (author): Added a brief note suggesting attaching `model_version` as an attribute to tracing spans.

Monica Patel (final): LGTM after CI is green.
release_notes:
- Python SDK now exposes `model_version` and `changelog_url` on response objects when returned by Redwood gateways.
- Docs/examples updated to show how to log resolved model versions and link to model release notes.
risk_assessment: Low. Additive fields only; behavior when headers are missing is unchanged. Streaming path relies on existing aggregation mechanism; covered by integration-style test.
